title: Edgecom component contracts
description: One contract per registry primitive: what it is for, what it may compose with, which tokens it reaches, and which states it supports. The primitives remain the authority — this is the compiled view of them, generated by scripts/gen-contracts.mjs and validated in CI so the docs, the registry and the Claude Design bundle cannot disagree about a component.

version.description: Git tag the contracts were built at, or 'untagged'.

digest.description: The identity of the whole design system — sha256 over the tokens, the design language, the primitives and the authored overlays, 16 hex chars — computed once in scripts/lib/system.mjs and stamped into every published artifact and into the design bundle's _system.json, so a design or an app built against a different digest is working from a different system. It changes when the system changes, not when a commit happens, so a committed copy stays parity-clean.

id.description: Section id; stable identifier for the component.

summary.description: One line, from curated.ts or the section blurb.

purpose.description: Authored: what the component is for, in the Edgecom product context.

useWhen.description: Authored: selection criteria — reach for it when these hold.

dontUseWhen.description: Authored: when a different component is the right answer, naming it.

base.description: The Base UI primitive underneath, when there is one. Base UI, never Radix.

variants.description: cva variant groups, read from the primitive. The authoritative list of what the component can look like.

states.description: Tailwind modifiers the primitive actually styles — hover, focus-visible, disabled, data-[state=open] and so on. Derived, so it cannot claim a state the component does not implement.

responsive.description: Breakpoints the primitive itself responds to. Empty means it is size-agnostic and its container decides.

tokens.description: Semantic tokens the component's classes reach. A consumer changing one of these changes this component.

requires.description: Authored: compositions that must be present for the component to be correct.

forbids.description: Authored: compositions that are wrong, and what to do instead.

rules.description: Authored: the usage rules published in the Claude Design spec for this component.

behavior.description: Authored: what the component does in each non-happy path. A key is absent when the state does not apply to this component.

attributes.description: Derived: roles and ARIA attributes the primitive already sets.

requirements.description: Authored: what the consumer still has to supply.

examples.description: Authored: canonical usages, as code or a one-line description.

antiPatterns.description: Authored: the mistakes seen in real designs and PRs, stated as the mistake.

status.description: Migration metadata. 'legacy' means it still ships but new work should not reach for it.

deprecated.description: What to migrate to, and why. Non-null requires status 'deprecated'.

authored.description: Whether a human has written this contract's purpose. False means the contract is the derived half only.

then.description: An authored contract states its purpose. The flag is derived from that field, so the two cannot disagree.
